findings.claim: THE ROOT CAUSE of the central mystery: clog 0.10.0 has an EMPTY built-in section/alias map. Commits are collected and parsed fine, but any commit whose type is not found in the user-supplied [sections] map is discarded, so with no [sections] the section list is empty and serializes as null. Supplying [sections] unblocks '####' and '* ' output. This is a config issue, NOT a repo-shape or environment issue.

`BREAKING CHANGE:` / `BREAKING-CHANGE:` / `BREAKING CHANGE:x` in the body are inert — they do not create a Breaks entry and do not set JSON `breaks`. The Breaks heading is only reachable via the commit TYPE plus a declared alias.

If -f is PRESENT (even with an empty string) or -F is present, clog passes exactly one range token "FROM..TO", with TO defaulting to the literal "HEAD".

findings.claim: BUG: `-o /dev/full` gets the process SIGKILLed (OOM) because clog READS the destination before writing -- /dev/full/dev/zero yield infinite zero bytes and it buffers them unbounded. Under a memory cap it degrades to exit 1 "fatal I/O error with output file".
